subStrands.name: History of Computers, Data and Information

objectives.description: History of computers: computing devices; concept of number system in computing; generations of computer — first, second, third, fourth, fifth generations — year of development, basic component/type of technology, speed of operation, storage capacity/component.
Data and information: definition of data and information; types of data; ways of handling data; digitalization; differences between data and information.

subStrands.name: Computer Classification, ICT Applications and Components

objectives.description: Classification of computers: by type, size and usage.
Application of ICT in everyday life: uses of ICT in everyday activities; impact of ICT in the society; areas of ICT application linked to societal development.
Components of computers: input devices, output devices, system unit, storage devices — examples of each component and how they are used in data processing.

subStrands.name: Information Processing, Transmission, Networking and Internet

objectives.description: The art of information processing: definition of information processing; steps involved in information processing.

Process of information transmission: definition of information transmission; methods of transmitting information; modes of information transmission — visuals (newspaper), audio (radio, telephone), audio-visual (GSM, television).
Medium of information transmission: types of information transmission; classification of means of transmission (radio, television, newspaper etc.).
Networking: meaning of networking, internet and intranet; types of networking — MAN, LAN, WAN; significance of networking.
Internet: definition; benefits of internet; internet browsers; internet security; abuse of the internet.

subStrands.name: Operating System, Word Processing, Spreadsheet, Database, Presentation, Web and Graphics

objectives.description: Operating system: definition, types, examples and functions of operating system; differences between text (character) base interface and graphical user interface (GUI).
Word processing: definition, uses and examples of word processing software; starting, loading and exiting word processing; creating, saving and retrieving documents.
Spreadsheet: definition, uses and examples of spreadsheet applications; loading and exiting spreadsheets; creating, saving and retrieving spreadsheet files.

Database management system: definition, uses and examples of database applications; loading and exiting DBMS; creating, saving and retrieving database files; examples of packages e.g. Microsoft Access.
Presentation package: definition, uses and examples; loading and exiting presentation programs; creating, saving and retrieving presentation files.
Web design packages: definition, uses, components and examples.
Graphic packages: definition, uses and examples of graphic packages (focus on Corel Draw).

strands.name: Computer Maintenance, Ethics and Data Management

subStrands.name: Maintenance, Ethics, Safety, Career and Data Management

objectives.description: Maintenance of computer: general cleaning; battery charging and replacement for portable systems and UPS; DVD drive lens cleaning; details of hardware maintenance; details of software maintenance; computer crash and data recovery.
Computer ethics: computer room management ethics; laboratory rules and regulations; responsible ways of using and securing computers.

Safety measures: sitting arrangement; positioning of the monitor, keyboard, CPU, mouse and peripheral devices; illuminating the computer room; maintaining a dust free environment; keeping liquid away from the computer room.
Career opportunities in data processing: professions in computer; qualities of a good data processing professional; computer professional bodies and their duties.
Computer virus: definition, types/examples, sources, signals of virus warning, virus prevention, detection and deletion; destructive effects of virus infection on computers.

Relational model: database and table creation using application packages; creating relationships between tables — primary and foreign keys, entities, attributes and relationships; creation of forms, queries and reports; query language (query by example, SQL).
File organization: definition and types of file organization; comparison between the various types of file organization.
Database security: concept of data security, access control and data encryption; role of a database administrator.
Parallel and distributed databases: basic concept of parallel and distributed database; storing data in a distributed database management system (DBM).
